mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or neutral in periods of CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or neutral in periods of UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above a 5% month-over-month growth rate signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative or neutral in periods of HOUST MoM > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below a 2% year-over-year growth rate signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or neutral in periods of INDPRO YoY < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which can lead to reduced consumer and business spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or neutral during periods of rising FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 signals strong job growth, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative or neutral in periods of PAYEMS > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above a 4% year-over-year growth rate signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative or neutral in periods of RSAFS YoY > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with monetary tightening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or neutral in periods of FEDFUNDS > 2% and UNRATE < 4%.
